cases.name: the id of True
cases.purpose: The canonical text of True is (C True) and the id is the FNV-1a hash of that text, as documentation/lean-meta.md says; the first call also shows that the server's project has SeshatMeta.

cases.name: bound names do not change the id
cases.purpose: (m : Nat) : m = m has the canonical text (P (C Nat) (A (C Eq (s 0)) (C Nat) #0 #0)), the same as (n : ℕ) : n = n, the manifest's example.

cases.name: binder kinds and instance paths do not change the id
cases.purpose: An implicit binder is written like an explicit one, and the instance arguments of HAdd.hAdd and OfNat.ofNat, closed, are written _: the canonical text is (P (C Nat) (A (C Eq (s 0)) (C Nat) (A (C HAdd.hAdd 0 0 0) (C Nat) (C Nat) (C Nat) _ #0 (A (C OfNat.ofNat 0) (C Nat) (N 0) _)) #0)).

cases.name: a statement about the header's definitions
cases.purpose: The header's own definitions elaborate before the command, after the imports and import SeshatMeta.

input.header:
import Mathlib

namespace Harness

def double (n : ℕ) : ℕ := n + n

end Harness

cases.name: a statement Lean refuses
cases.purpose: An elaboration error fails the call with Lean's message, and no id.

cases.name: definitionally equal statements
cases.purpose: n + 0 reduces to n, so isDefEq says true.

cases.name: different statements
cases.purpose: isDefEq says false when the statements differ.

cases.name: the premises of a proof
cases.purpose: The theorems a proof term uses, and only theorems.

input.code:
import Mathlib

theorem Harness.swap (a b : ℕ) : a + b = b + a := Nat.add_comm a b

cases.name: the structure profile of a statement
cases.purpose: The class of an instance binder, the classes of instance arguments, and the instances used.

cases.name: a fact a statement is an instance of
cases.purpose: The discrimination tree finds the commutativity of addition for 2 + 3 = 3 + 2, unification confirms it, and the fact about multiplication is not a candidate.

facts.name: add_comm_nat
facts.statement: (a b : ℕ) : a + b = b + a

cases.name: the statements a fact covers
cases.purpose: The other direction: a general statement covers its instances, and a hypothesis of the general one is closed by the instance's own.

input.statement: (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) : a < b + 1
